newsitem.title: USA: Court dismisses most Florida tobacco claims.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses most Florida tobacco claims.

text.p: A circuit judge late on Monday dismissed all the pre-1994 claims in the Medicaid suit brought against the tobacco industry by the state of Florida, Philip Morris Cos Inc said.
The court ruled that a recent state Supreme Court decision held that those claims could not go forward under the 1994 Florida Medicaid Amendments, Philip Morris said.
In his decision, Circuit Judge Harold Cohen also threw out 15 of the state's 18 claims against the cigarette companies.

The court threw out the same damage claims that have been asserted by other states that have filed similar Medicaid reimbursement lawsuits, including restitution, fraud, and conspiracy, Philip Morris said.
On the three remaining claims for damages, the court held that the state could not proceed without identifying each individual recipient of Medicaid payments.

The Florida case "provided the most significant test of the states' legal attempts to impose liability on the tobacco industry without introducing proof of individual smoking," the company said in a statement accompanying the announcement.
The decision effectively means that states must prove their cases on an individual-by-individual basis.

"Subject to the state's ability to identify individual recipients, the state is permitted to go forward with its post-1994 claims for negligence, product liability, and injunctive relief," Philip Morris said.
Those claims will be restricted to the state's ability to prove damages that were incurred since July 1, 1994, when the Florida Medicaid Amendments took effect.

"Today's decision is a significant victory for the industry and should provide a compelling basis for the dismissal of similar claims in other states where attorneys general are seeking to misuse the courts to legislate new and unprecedented legal theories," said Gregory Little, senior assistant general counsel for Philip Morris, in a press release.
